article.headline: Free Blender Plugin Brings Local AI Motion Capture to Consumer GPUs
article.lede: For most independent animators, capturing convincing human movement has meant either expensive hardware suits or laborious hand-keying frame by frame. CyanPuppets, a Guangzhou startup, has released a free Blender plugin that uses a locally-run neural model to extract full-body, hand, and facial data from an ordinary webcam in real time — no cloud upload, no subscription required for non-commercial use.
article.body:
CyanPuppets was founded in 2019 by a team with roots at Tencent (0700.HK) and has since built its technology around a proprietary **1-billion-parameter** neural model — a notable clarification, since a widely circulated description of the tool (including one prominent Facebook post) erroneously inflated the figure to ten billion. The model weighs roughly 4.2 GB and runs entirely on the user's hardware, requiring a GPU with at least 8 GB of *VRAM* (video memory). An NVIDIA RTX 3060 is the stated minimum for real-time capture; the underlying inference engine is compatible with AMD and Intel GPUs as well.

The pipeline extracts **208 skeletal key points** per frame: 33 covering the full body and limbs, 21 per hand, and 140 for facial expressions. At 30 to 50 frames per second, it streams pose data into Blender via the *VMC protocol* — a lightweight UDP-based signaling standard that originated in Japanese virtual-streamer culture — through a companion add-on called *VMC4B*. Claimed latency is under 100 milliseconds. The same data stream can simultaneously feed Unreal Engine or Unity.

The free tier is limited to non-commercial use; a Personal licence runs $50 per month and an Enterprise tier $1,499 per year. That pricing undercuts cloud-based rivals: Rokoko Vision and DeepMotion both charge subscription fees and impose per-minute upload caps, and reviewers consistently describe their output as noisier and less stable than local alternatives. The fully local approach also avoids the privacy friction of sending motion footage to a third-party server.

CyanPuppets counts Bilibili (BILI) among its enterprise partners and is enrolled in NVIDIA's (NVDA) INCEPTION programme for AI startups. The plugin exports FBX files compatible with a wide range of rigs — MetaHuman, Mixamo, Daz, VRM, and others — which lowers the barrier to entry considerably. Meaningful constraints remain: the software runs on Windows 10 only, demands 100 GB of storage, and the company's own benchmarks put average limb error at roughly 3 centimetres, a figure that places it firmly in the prototyping-and-reference tier rather than production-ready *performance capture*.

concepts.definition: Video RAM — dedicated memory on a graphics card used to store textures, frame buffers, and, increasingly, the weights of locally-run AI models. A model that demands 8 GB of VRAM will not run at all on a GPU with less, regardless of how much system RAM the computer has.

A method of recording human movement using only cameras and computer vision, without physical reflective markers or sensors attached to the performer's body. Traditional studio mocap requires a suit covered in markers; markerless approaches infer skeleton position from video pixels alone, trading some precision for dramatically lower cost and setup time.

Virtual Motion Capture protocol — a lightweight, open messaging standard (transmitted over UDP) originally developed for Japanese virtual-streamer workflows. It encodes skeleton bone positions and rotations as OSC (Open Sound Control) messages, allowing different applications to share live pose data in real time.

A Blender add-on that acts as a VMC protocol receiver, translating incoming skeleton data from an external capture application into bone rotations on a Blender armature. It serves as the bridge between CyanPuppets' standalone capture software and Blender's animation system.

Specific anatomical landmarks — joints, fingertips, facial landmarks — that a pose-estimation model predicts from image data. Each key point is expressed as a 3-D coordinate; connecting them produces a skeleton that can drive a character rig.

A higher-fidelity form of motion capture that records not just body movement but also subtle facial acting and finger detail simultaneously, as used in films and AAA video games. It typically requires professional studios and is distinct from the lighter 'body-only' capture used for blocking and reference.

Compute Unified Device Architecture — NVIDIA's proprietary parallel-computing platform and API, which allows software developers to run general-purpose computations on NVIDIA GPUs. Most commercial AI inference frameworks are optimised for CUDA first, with AMD and Intel GPU support added later.

Filmbox — a proprietary 3-D interchange file format owned by Autodesk and widely used to transfer animated character data (meshes, skeletons, keyframes) between different 3-D applications such as Blender, Maya, Unreal Engine, and Unity.

article.fact_check: A widely shared Facebook post (by Hypermatter/Ahmed Abdallah Madkour) and at least one other secondary source describe the underlying AI model as having '10 billion parameters.' Every official CyanPuppets communication — product pages, social posts, press coverage — consistently specifies 1 billion parameters. The tweet under review does not make the 10-billion claim; the 8 GB VRAM figure and the dual live/upload capture modes it cites are accurate.

ticker_0700-hk.name: Tencent Holdings Limited
ticker_0700-hk.blurb: Tencent Holdings Limited is an investment holding company that provides value-added services, marketing services, fintech, and business services in Mainland China and internationally. Its consumer business includes communications and social services (instant messaging and social networks), digital content (online games, videos, live streaming, news, music, and literature), fintech services (mobile payment, wealth management, consumer loans, and securities trading), and various tools. Tencent is one of the world's largest internet and technology companies by revenue and market capitalization, with a dominant position in China's social media and gaming markets.
ticker_0700-hk.recent: In the past 30 days, Tencent's stock price has shown volatility, trading in a range of approximately 460 to 480 HKD. The company is scheduled to report earnings on May 13, 2026, with analysts expecting continued revenue growth driven by its fintech and gaming segments. Recent news highlights include regulatory developments in China's tech sector and Tencent's ongoing investments in AI and cloud computing.

ticker_bili.name: Bilibili Inc.
ticker_bili.blurb: Bilibili Inc. is a leading Chinese online entertainment platform that offers a wide range of content including video streaming, live broadcasting, and mobile games. It is particularly popular among Generation Z users in China, known for its community-driven ecosystem and bullet-commenting feature. The company generates revenue through mobile games, value-added services, advertising, and e-commerce. Bilibili competes with other Chinese video platforms like iQiyi and Tencent Video, and has been expanding its content offerings to include more professional and original programming.
ticker_bili.recent: In the past 30 days, Bilibili's stock has experienced volatility amid broader market concerns about Chinese regulatory crackdowns and economic slowdown. The company reported mixed quarterly earnings, with revenue growth slowing but user engagement metrics remaining strong. Analysts have noted potential catalysts from new game approvals and advertising recovery, though near-term outlook remains cautious.

ticker_nvda.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ticker_nvda.blurb: NVIDIA designs graphics processing units (GPUs) and system-on-chip products. Originally a gaming chip company, it became the dominant supplier of AI accelerators — chips that perform the parallel matrix math required to train and run large language models. Its H100, H200, and Blackwell GPU families are the de facto standard for AI training infrastructure at hyperscalers and cloud providers. NVIDIA's CUDA software ecosystem creates deep switching costs: virtually all AI frameworks and models are optimised for CUDA, making competing hardware difficult to adopt at scale. NVIDIA also sells networking (InfiniBand, Ethernet) and data-centre systems.
ticker_nvda.recent: NVIDIA reported FY2026 (ending Jan 2026) revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% YoY, with data centre revenue reaching $186 billion. The company's forward P/E of ~17.5x on 34.8% projected EPS growth produces a PEG of 0.50 — unusually cheap for what is arguably the most critical infrastructure company in the AI buildout. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) collectively committed over $200 billion in AI infrastructure capex for 2026, the majority flowing through NVIDIA's supply chain.
